thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'pool-rush-03' p99 latency spike > 4s (streaming stalls observed). Autoscale attempted + warmup delay > 90s. Paging on-call.
alice_sre: I'm on it. seeing queue depth jump on pool-rush-03, warmup_success rate is low. Any live customer impact metrics?
frank-cs: Support reports ~3 customers on dedicated capacity experiencing streaming disconnects and tail latency spikes. One internal customer reports timeouts in video-captioning pipeline.
eva_support: Customer A (acct-453) seeing 12% timeout rate for streaming endpoints, started ~10:42 UTC. Logged ticket INC-8792.
carla_oncall: Reassigning to runtime to check autoscaler handshake and GPU init logs. ben_runtime, dmitri_eng please triage.
ben_runtime: pulling logs. early signs: warmup pod init stuck at model load step, repeated OOM during quantize stage on node-12. kube shows several pods in CrashLoopBackOff.
ben_runtime: snippets:
```
2026-03-14T10:42:31Z model-loader: loading shard 5/8
2026-03-14T10:42:34Z runtime: OOM while allocating KV cache (requested 1.6GB)
2026-03-14T10:42:34Z pod: restarting
```
dmitri_eng: That OOM explains long warmup. Did autoscaler provision smaller instance type accidentally? checking pool config.
dmitri_eng: pool-rush-03 autoscaler policy shows node-type fallback to gpu-xsmall under burst — that's incompatible with model size. Patch: policy should prefer gpu-large. suspect a recent policy change in PR #4123.
alice_sre: For immediate mitigation: 1) disable autoscale fallback to xsmall for pool-rush-03 2) manually scale up 2 gpu-large nodes 3) reroute new streaming sessions to hosted-fallback pool. Who can run manual scale now?
ben_runtime: I can scale. Running:
```
redwoodctl pool scale --pool pool-rush-03 --count +2 --node-type gpu-large
```
ben_runtime: executed, cluster accepted request, provisioning started.
carla_oncall: Re-route plan: add temporary routing rule to divert new requests for model "llama-65b-q" to hosted-fallback-01 for accounts with <= 5k qps. This avoids cold starts in dedicated pool.
dmitri_eng: Confirmed the autoscaler policy PR reverted in staging but not prod. I'll roll a hotfix to remove xsmall fallback and add a safety check for model memory before choosing node type.
frank-cs: Notifying affected customers: short message drafted to A/B group pointing at degraded streaming; ETA to restore ~15-25m.
eva_support: Sending message to ACCTS: 453, 688, 944. Also creating incident status page update.
alice_sre: Observability: p95 is stable but p99 still elevated. After scale request we see warmup tasks starting. KV cache warmup still slow for some shards.
ben_runtime: Warmup pods are now initializing on gpu-large nodes. But model-loader still occasionally OOMs on shard 8. Increasing ephemeral swap allowed on those nodes as temporary relief.
ben_runtime: Applied sysctl tweak to increase vm.overcommit_memory for nodes provisioned.
dmitri_eng: Rolling out hotfix to autoscaler in 1min. Will also add a preflight memory check to avoid selecting undersized nodes.
carla_oncall: After routing change, request rate to pool-rush-03 dropped by ~60%. Streaming disconnects for most customers reduced dramatically.
alice_sre: Can we get a rough impact tally? frank-cs/eva_support?
frank-cs: Initial: ~3 tenants impacted, combined ~2.2k streaming sessions; estimate 7% of global streaming requests during the window impacted. No PII exposure.
eva_support: Customers acknowledged the update, one asked for log bundle for their team. Filing follow-ups.
ben_runtime: p99 down to 1.8s from 4.2s for non-affected routes. Streaming reconnect attempts still sticky for sessions that hit OOM during warmup — need session-level graceful retry support in client.
dmitri_eng: Hotfix deployed. Autoscaler will now refuse gpu-xsmall for any model >32B and will mark node-type as incompatible in pool config. Creating post-deploy monitor to ensure no regression.
alice_sre: Action items during incident:
- manual scale +2 gpu-large (done)
- routing rule to hosted-fallback (done)
- hotfix autoscaler policy (deployed)
- collect kernel + dmesg logs from nodes that OOMed (ben)
- support notifications (eva/frank)
- create postmortem (carla)
carla_oncall: I'll start the postmortem doc and include timeline and customer impact. Assigning owner: carla_oncall. Target draft in 24h.
ben_runtime: uploading logs to /var/reports/incidents/2171112223/logs.tar.gz and attaching to ticket INC-8792.
frank-cs: Follow-up with customers: offering extended credits and a sync if they'd like deep dive.
alice_sre: Closing notes: keep pool pinned to gpu-large for next 72h while we validate autoscaler preflight. Schedule an audit of recent policy PRs that touch fallback logic.
dmitri_eng: I'll add an integration test that emulates model-size -> node-type selection to catch this earlier.
carla_oncall: Marking incident status=mitigated. Will change to resolved after postmortem & follow-ups.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, responders=[alice_sre, ben_runtime, dmitri_eng, carla_oncall, eva_support, frank-cs], timeline_url=https://redwood.status/incidents/2171112223
alice_sre: Thanks all :thumbsup: Great triage and fast manual mitigation.
